newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Heavy bank withdrawals send Pakistan rates up.
newsitem.headline: Heavy bank withdrawals send Pakistan rates up.

text.p: Large-scale withdrawals from banks caused by a loss of confidence in the economy have sent Pakistani money rates and yields on six-month federal bonds soaring, financial market dealers said on Tuesday.
"The liquidity crunch is the result of heavy withdrawals from bank deposits as investor confidence has ebbed during the past few weeks," dealer Salman Baig at KASB & Co said.

Political uncertainty, bad economic figures, the International Monetary Fund's delay in paying installments of a $600 million standby loan and a possible downgrading of Pakistan's credit rating had undermined investor confidence, one banker said.

With interbank rates for overnight and one-week funds soaring to 17 percent and above, banks were approaching the discounting window of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to square their positions, Baig said.
"Banks are discounting six to eight billion rupees ($162 to $216 billion) daily since last week, which is a record and shows the amount by which the market is short," he added.

Baig said Monday's auction of six-month federal bonds, at which the SBP accepted only 53.225 million rupees in bids at a weighted average of 13.6406 percent a year, showed that the central bank itself was running short of funds.
